strings.wudu_d_blood_p1: Blood or pus breaks it once it flows past the wound; vomit breaks it when it comes up as a mouthful.
strings.wudu_d_blood_p1_src: Nur al-Idah, Book i: Purification — Nullifications of Wudu
strings.wudu_d_blood_p2_src: Reliance of the Traveller, e7.5; The Risala (Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani), 2.2p
strings.wudu_d_blood_p3: Breaks it if the discharge — blood, pus and the like — is copious enough to be repugnant; a small amount does not.
strings.wudu_d_blood_p3_src: Umdat al-Fiqh (Ibn Qudamah), Book 1 ch. 6: The Nullifiers of Wudu
strings.wudu_d_dalak_p1: Not obligatory — water reaching the skin is enough. The Hanafi school still counts rubbing a recommended sunna.
strings.wudu_d_dalak_p1_src: Nur al-Idah, Book i: Purification — The Sunan of Wudu; Reliance of the Traveller, e5.1; Umdat al-Fiqh (Ibn Qudamah), Book 1 ch. 4: Wudu
strings.wudu_d_dalak_p2: Obligatory (fard). The Risala has you wash each limb “with both hands”; its commentary states plainly that rubbing the limb is required in itself, not merely letting water run over it.
strings.wudu_d_dalak_subject: Whether dalak (rubbing the limbs) is obligatory.
strings.wudu_d_head_p1: At least a quarter of the head.
strings.wudu_d_head_p1_src: Nur al-Idah, Book i: Purification — The Pillars of Wudu
strings.wudu_d_head_p2: Any part of the head suffices, even a small portion.
strings.wudu_d_head_p3_src: The Risala (Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani), 4.6t; Umdat al-Fiqh (Ibn Qudamah), Book 1 ch. 4: Wudu
strings.wudu_d_head_subject: How much of the head must be wiped.
strings.wudu_d_istinshaq_p1: A sunna in wudu, but obligatory (fard) in the ghusl, on the same reasoning as rinsing the mouth.
strings.wudu_d_istinshaq_p1_src: Nur al-Idah, Book i: Purification — The Sunan of Wudu; Nur al-Idah, Book i: Purification — That Which Is Compulsory To Wash
strings.wudu_d_istinshaq_p2_src: Reliance of the Traveller, e5.1, e5.7; The Risala (Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani), 4.4, 40.01
strings.wudu_d_istinshaq_p3: Obligatory in both the wudu and the ghusl, like rinsing the mouth.
strings.wudu_d_istinshaq_p3_src: Umdat al-Fiqh (Ibn Qudamah), Book 1 ch. 4: Wudu; Umdat al-Fiqh (Ibn Qudamah), Book 1 ch. 7: Major Ablution (For Major Sexual Ritual Impurity)
strings.wudu_d_istinshaq_subject: The ruling of istinshaq and istinthar in wudu and in ghusl.
strings.wudu_d_madmadah_p1: A sunna in wudu, but obligatory (fard) in the ghusl — the mouth counts among the parts the ghusl verse requires be washed.
strings.wudu_d_madmadah_p1_src: Nur al-Idah, Book i: Purification — The Sunan of Wudu; Nur al-Idah, Book i: Purification — That Which Is Compulsory To Wash
strings.wudu_d_madmadah_p2_src: Reliance of the Traveller, e5.1, e5.7; The Risala (Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani), 4.4, 40.01
strings.wudu_d_madmadah_p3: Obligatory in both the wudu and the ghusl; the manual notes that the other three schools count it only preferable.
strings.wudu_d_madmadah_p3_src: Umdat al-Fiqh (Ibn Qudamah), Book 1 ch. 4: Wudu; Umdat al-Fiqh (Ibn Qudamah), Book 1 ch. 7: Major Ablution (For Major Sexual Ritual Impurity)
strings.wudu_d_madmadah_subject: The ruling of madmadah in wudu and in ghusl.
strings.wudu_d_muwalat_p1: A sunna, not fard. An unbroken sequence is recommended; a pause, even a long one, leaves the wudu valid and needs no fresh intention.
strings.wudu_d_muwalat_p1_src: Nur al-Idah, Book i: Purification — The Sunan of Wudu; Reliance of the Traveller, e5.17
strings.wudu_d_muwalat_p2: This guide does not state a Maliki position here. The Risala lists four obligations for the wudu — the face, the hands, wiping the head, and the feet — and does not treat continuity among them or anywhere else in its chapter on wudu. Ask someone who teaches this school.
strings.wudu_d_muwalat_p3: Fard — one of the mandatory acts: no washed part may be left to dry before the next is reached.
strings.wudu_d_muwalat_p3_src: Umdat al-Fiqh (Ibn Qudamah), Book 1 ch. 4: Wudu
strings.wudu_d_niyyah_p1: A sunna, not fard. Wudu made without a settled intention is still valid; what is lost is the reward, not the ablution.
strings.wudu_d_niyyah_p1_src: Nur al-Idah, Book i: Purification — The Sunan of Wudu
strings.wudu_d_niyyah_p3: Obligatory. The Risala itself only says to perform wudu sincerely for Allah; its commentary states that intention being obligatory is agreed, and that it must accompany the start of washing the face.
strings.wudu_d_niyyah_p4: Fard. It is listed first among the mandatory acts, and wudu is not valid without it.
strings.wudu_d_niyyah_p4_src: Umdat al-Fiqh (Ibn Qudamah), Book 1 ch. 4: Wudu
strings.wudu_d_sleep_p1: Breaks it when one sleeps lying down — on the side, back or hip — where the joints go slack. Sleeping while firmly seated, or in a posture of the prayer, does not; nor does a light doze in which one still hears those nearby.
strings.wudu_d_sleep_p1_src: Nur al-Idah, Book i: Purification — Nullifications of Wudu
strings.wudu_d_sleep_p2: Breaks it unless one is sitting firmly. A light doze — in which one can still hear those nearby — does not break it in any position.
strings.wudu_d_sleep_p2_src: Reliance of the Traveller, e7.2; Umdat al-Fiqh (Ibn Qudamah), Book 1 ch. 6: The Nullifiers of Wudu
strings.wudu_d_sleep_p3: Breaks it whenever the sleep is deep, in any position. A doze in which one is aware of what is going on does not.
strings.wudu_d_tartib_p1: A sunna, not fard. Keeping to the Qur’an’s order is recommended, but the wudu is valid without it.
strings.wudu_d_tartib_p1_src: Nur al-Idah, Book i: Purification — The Sunan of Wudu
strings.wudu_d_tartib_p3: A sunna, not fard. The Risala places the order of the acts among the parts of wudu it calls “sunna”, not among its obligations.
strings.wudu_d_tartib_p4: Fard (obligatory) — one of the mandatory acts.
strings.wudu_d_tartib_p4_src: Umdat al-Fiqh (Ibn Qudamah), Book 1 ch. 4: Wudu
strings.wudu_d_touchself_p1_src: Nur al-Idah, Book i: Purification — That Which Does Not Nullify Wudu
strings.wudu_d_touchself_p2: Breaks it if the human private parts are touched with the palm or the inner surface of the fingers, one’s own or another’s.
strings.wudu_d_touchself_p3: Breaks it. In the Maliki school this means touching one’s own private part with the palm or inner fingers; the Hanbali school includes another person’s as well.
strings.wudu_d_touchself_p3_src: The Risala (Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani), 2.2n; Umdat al-Fiqh (Ibn Qudamah), Book 1 ch. 6: The Nullifiers of Wudu
strings.wudu_d_touchself_subject: Whether touching the private parts breaks wudu.
strings.wudu_d_touchwoman_p1: The touch itself does not break it. Any madhy it brings on does, but as a discharge from the private parts, not as a consequence of the touch.
strings.wudu_d_touchwoman_p1_src: Nur al-Idah, Book i: Purification — That Which Does Not Nullify Wudu; Nur al-Idah, Book i: Purification — Nullifications of Wudu
strings.wudu_d_touchwoman_p2: Breaks it when a man touches a non-mahram woman, with or without desire, and whichever of them does the touching.
strings.wudu_d_touchwoman_p3: Breaks it if the touch is done for pleasure, or brings it. A touch with neither does not.
strings.wudu_d_touchwoman_p3_src: The Risala (Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani), 2.2l; Umdat al-Fiqh (Ibn Qudamah), Book 1 ch. 6: The Nullifiers of Wudu
strings.wudu_d_touchwoman_subject: Whether touching a woman breaks wudu.
strings.wudu_hadith_edition: Hadith numbering follows the numbering used on Sunnah.com, which generally aligns with widely published editions.
strings.wudu_intro: Wudu is a prerequisite for the validity of prayer. This guide sets out what is required, what is recommended, and what breaks it.
strings.wudu_s1_1_detail: The firm resolve in the heart to perform wudu for the sake of Allah, or to enable prayer. Saying the intention aloud is not required. The intention must be made when you begin washing the face — not before, and not after.
strings.wudu_s1_2_detail: Wash the entire face: lengthwise from the hairline to the underside of the chin, widthwise from ear to ear, until water reaches all the skin.
strings.wudu_s1_3_detail: From the fingertips up to and including the elbows.
strings.wudu_s1_3_title: Washing the hands up to the elbows
strings.wudu_s1_4_detail: Passing wet hands over the head.
strings.wudu_s1_5_detail: From the toes up to and including the ankles.
strings.wudu_s1_5_title: Washing the feet up to the ankles
strings.wudu_s1_6_detail: Performing the obligatory acts in the sequence given in the verse: face, then hands, then head, then feet.
strings.wudu_s1_7_detail: Washing the limbs one after another, without letting the previous limb dry before washing the next.
strings.wudu_s1_body: These are the acts without which wudu is invalid. They are performed in the order given in the Qur’an — though whether that order, and continuity between them, are themselves obligatory varies by school.
strings.wudu_s1_heading: The acts of wudu, and which are required
strings.wudu_s2_beard_detail: Ensuring water reaches the skin beneath the beard.
strings.wudu_s2_beard_title: Takhleel al-lihyah (running wet fingers through a thick beard)
strings.wudu_s2_body: These increase reward and complete the wudu, but wudu is valid without them.
strings.wudu_s2_dalak_detail: Rubbing each limb with the hand while washing it.
strings.wudu_s2_dua_src: Sahih Muslim 234; addition in Sunan al-Tirmidhi 55
strings.wudu_s2_ears_detail: Outer and inner, with fresh water or what remains from wiping the head.
strings.wudu_s2_exaggerate_detail: For someone who is not fasting.
strings.wudu_s2_exaggerate_title: Going thoroughly in madmadah and istinshaq
strings.wudu_s2_fingers_title: Takhleel al-asabi’ (working water between the fingers and toes)
strings.wudu_s2_hands3_detail: Before putting them into a vessel, if one is used.
strings.wudu_s2_istinshaq_title: Istinshaq and istinthar (drawing water into the nose and expelling it)
strings.wudu_s2_right_detail: When washing the hands and the feet.
strings.wudu_s2_tasmiyah_src: Sunan Abi Dawud 101; Sunan Ibn Majah 399. Scholars differ on the authenticity of this wording; tasmiyah is widely held to be an emphasised sunnah.
strings.wudu_s3_1_detail: Urine, faeces, wind, madhy (pre-seminal fluid), wady (prostatic fluid).
strings.wudu_s3_1_title: Anything leaving the two private parts
strings.wudu_s3_2_detail: Sleep in which awareness is lost.
strings.wudu_s3_2_src: Sunan Abi Dawud 203; Sunan Ibn Majah 477
strings.wudu_s3_3_detail: Such as fainting, insanity or intoxication — by analogy with deep sleep, being a more complete loss of awareness.
strings.wudu_s3_4_title: Touching the private parts directly, with no barrier
strings.wudu_s3_5_title: A man touching a non-mahram woman
strings.wudu_s3_6_title: Blood, pus or vomit leaving the body other than from the private parts
strings.wudu_s3_body: These nullify wudu, and it must be performed again.
strings.wudu_s4_1: Not washing a limb completely — leaving part of the elbows, ankles or heels dry.
strings.wudu_s4_2: Using far more water than needed, which is disliked.
strings.wudu_s4_3: Not keeping to the order, which matters most for those whose school holds it obligatory.
strings.wudu_s4_4: Not letting water reach every part — for example not moving a ring or a watch.
strings.wudu_s4_5: Skipping wiping the ears, which is a sunnah many people overlook.
strings.wudu_s5_agree_1: Washing the entire face is obligatory.
strings.wudu_s5_agree_2: Washing the hands up to the elbows is obligatory.
strings.wudu_s5_agree_3: Wiping the head is obligatory (they differ on how much).
strings.wudu_s5_agree_4: Washing the feet up to the ankles is obligatory.
strings.wudu_s5_agree_5: Anything leaving the two private parts breaks wudu.
strings.wudu_s5_agree_6: Deep sleep breaks wudu, with slight variation in how it is defined.
strings.wudu_s5_agree_body: All four Sunni schools agree on:
strings.wudu_s5_differ_body: They differ on the points marked in this guide: niyyah, tartib, muwalat, how much of the head is wiped, madmadah and istinshaq, dalak, touching the private parts, touching a non-mahram woman, blood and vomit, and the conditions under which sleep breaks wudu.
strings.wudu_s5_heading: What the schools agree and differ on
strings.wudu_src_nur: Nur al-Idah, Hasan al-Shurunbulali — Hanafi. Book i (Purification) was read directly for this guide.
strings.wudu_src_reliance: Reliance of the Traveller (Umdat al-Salik), Ahmad ibn Naqib al-Misri, tr. Nuh Ha Mim Keller — Shafi’i. Book e (Purification) was read directly for this guide.
strings.wudu_src_risala: The Risala, Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani, tr. Bello Mohammad Daura, with the commentary of al-Azhari — Maliki. Chapters 2 and 4 were read directly for this guide.
strings.wudu_src_umdah: Umdat al-Fiqh, Ibn Qudamah al-Maqdisi, translated with commentary by Hatem al-Haj — Hanbali. Book 1 (Purification) was read directly for this guide.
strings.wudu_unreviewed: This guide has NOT yet been checked by a qualified scholar. It is a draft. Do not rely on it for how to pray until this notice is removed.
